author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Balkh; the Bâlâ-Hisâr is the 'royal city' of the Chinese pilgrims
evidence: Survey of the Balkh ramparts (1924): the oval Bâlâ-Hisâr enclosure under the Arg is the Greek Basileion and the pilgrims' 'royal city', with the artisans' town to its south.
quote: elle représente non moins clairement le Basileion des Grecs et la « ville royale » des pèlerins chinois
note: Agrees (Balkh). Adds that the pilgrims' royal city is the Bâlâ-Hisâr enclosure.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the 200-ft stupa of the Nava-saṅghârâma = Tôp-é-Rustam, SW of old Balkh
evidence: His own excavation (28 Jan.–14 May 1924) proved Tôp-é-Rustam a Buddhist stupa, restored before 630. It lies SW of the old city (Burj-é-'Ayârân = SW corner) on the old road out of the Nau-behâr gate, and is the only tôp there. He admits the stupa/vihâra layout does not match the text.
quote: Hiuan-tsang, toujours soucieux de la propriété des termes dont il se sert, écrit correctement : Nava-sanghārama … il s'ensuit que la charge de la preuve incomberait à qui nierait l'identité de notre stûpa avec celui qui a l'honneur de figurer dans le Si-yu-ki
note: Agrees: this is the source of the study's 'probably Top-i-Rustam'. Foucher himself notes that Takht-é-Rustam does not fit the text and that the monastery and vihâra are not found, so the identification rests on the stupa alone.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: not located; to be sought NW of Balkh, near the Kelif road
evidence: Planned in 1924 but not carried out. Direction from the text ('NW' of Balkh).
quote: aller chercher à quelque distance « dans le Nord-Ouest » de Balkh, sans doute aux abords de la route de Kélif, les deux stûpa anciens que la tradition locale, retenue par Hiuan-tsang, attribuait aux deux grands marchands Trapusha et Bhallika
note: Agrees that the place is unlocated; adds a search area (Kelif road NW of Balkh).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Buddhist rock-cut stupa and cave monastery 3 km NW of Haibak; Xuanzang did not pass Haibak
evidence: Visited 1924: unfinished monolithic stupa ('Takht-é-Rustam') and five caves (chapels, dormitory, assembly hall). His route of Xuanzang goes up the Balkh-âb and Darrah-Yûsuf, joining the modern road only at the Qarâ-kotal.
quote: A la vérité, Haibâk se trouvait jadis à l'écart de la grand-route de l'Inde, telle que Hiuan-tsang l'a suivie, de Bactres à Peshâwar … le pèlerin n'a-t-il pas visité cette localité
note: Adds a Buddhist site at the study's capital of 01.30 (Haibak), but Foucher does not connect it with 紇露悉泯健. He holds that Xuanzang did not go through Haibak, which fits 01.30 being a country he describes but did not visit.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: old Khulm ruins near Tâsh-Qurghân
evidence: The nearly abandoned ruins of old Khulm show the town's antiquity; not linked to Xuanzang's text.
quote: les ruines voisines, aujourd'hui presque abandonnées au désert, du vieux Khulm attestent l'antique importance de cette cité
note: Agrees with Mizutani's ruins N of Tashkurgan, but gives no argument from Xuanzang.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Darrah-Gâz ('Valley of the Tamarisks') on the Balkh-âb; Xuanzang's road up the Balkh-âb and Darrah-Yûsuf
evidence: Route: the old Balkh–Bâmyân road went up the Balkh-âb and its right-bank tributary in the Darrah-Yûsuf to the Qarâ-kotal. The 'ten monasteries' are placed along the Balkh-âb; none were visited.
quote: Adoptant la vallée du Balkh-âb et le Darrah-Yûsuf … « quelque dix couvents » signalés par Hiuan-tsang le long du Balkh-âb dans le pays de Kie-tche (aujourd'hui le Darrah-Gâz ou Vallée des Tamaris)
note: Agrees (Darrah Gaz, up the Darrah Yusuf).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Tâlikân of Khurâsân, 3 days E of Merv-er-rûd and 2 days W of Maimaneh; not the Tâliqân E of Kunduz
evidence: Arabic geographers (Le Strange). It marks the Sasanian–Tokharistan border on the Murgh-âb.
quote: du royaume de Ta-la-kien, c'est-à-dire de l'ancien Tālikan … Ce Tālikan ne doit donc pas être confondu avec celui qui subsiste à l'Est de Kunduz
note: Agrees (Ṭālaqān of Khurāsān near Maimana); he does not name a ruin.

author: A. Foucher
name_in_asr: Bâmyân: ancient town, the two standing Buddhas
asr_identification: old town begins c. 1.5 km before the 53 m Buddha, astride the road and river; the 35 m Buddha was the 'brass' one
evidence: Visits of 1922 and 1923, with Pelliot's retranslation. The 35 m Buddha is stone finished in stucco; Xuanzang's 'brass' is explained as a metal sheathing in 630.
quote: Elle nous a paru commencer à environ un kilomètre et demi avant d'arriver au Buddha de 53 mètres … le plus petit (et le plus ancien) des deux Buddhas debout — celui de « plus de cent pieds », et en effet il mesure 35 mètres — était, nous dit-il, en laiton
note: Agrees (53 m and 35 m Buddhas); adds the location of the town, NE of which the cliff lies, and a reading of 鍮石 as metal sheathing.

author: A. Foucher
name_in_asr: Buddha couché de mille pieds; Ajdahâ
asr_identification: the reclining-Buddha monastery c. 1 km E of the town, at the E end of the Buddha cliff where a large ravine opens; the image was built of clay and pebbles
evidence: Pelliot's retranslation (E of the town, not W). Foucher withdraws his earlier identification with the Ajdahâ rock (300 m, W of Bâmyân), which he still holds was a Buddhist pilgrimage place, but not the one Xuanzang names.
quote: que nous avions d'abord cru devoir identifier avec les 300 mètres bien comptés du rocher qui s'appelle aujourd'hui Ajdahâ … prouve qu'il faut chercher cette reproduction artificielle de la statue svayambhû à l'endroit où l'extrémité orientale de la « falaise des grands Buddhas » vient mourir
note: Differs from the study's note, which reports Foucher's emendation (W 12 li, natural rock). In 1942 Foucher dropped it and reads the text literally (E, c. 1 km), at the E end of the cliff. This removes the main support for a western site.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: 200 li SE of the reclining-Buddha monastery via Topchi, Kalû and the Hajigak pass, near Gardan-Divâl on the upper Helmand; Hackin: Sar-é-Cheshmeh (E side of the Unai pass)
evidence: Pelliot's reading SE (not Julien's SW); road distances in krur: reclining Buddha–Topchi 5, –Kalû 9, –Gardan-Divâl 10 = c. 70 km = 210 li. Hackin's unpublished alternative, Sar-é-Cheshmeh, has a sacred fish pool.
quote: met, en effet, hors de doute que cette excursion de 200 li s'est faite au « Sud-Est » … de Kalû à Gardan-Divâl, sur le haut Hélmand, 10 : soit au total 24 krur ou environ 70 kilomètres = 210 li
note: Supports the literal-SE option (Gardan-Diwal, upper Helmand), not Fondukistan. Adds Hackin's Sar-é-Cheshmeh at the Kabul river source as a second candidate.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the highway left Bâmyân by the Ghorband (Shibar), but Xuanzang left it and was lost; Hackin: lost in the Paghman mountains coming from Sar-é-Cheshmeh
evidence: Route reasoning: in the 7th c. the highway still went down the Ghorband. Xuanzang knew the Kalû–Hajigak branch at Shahr-é-Zohâk. On Hackin's view of 01.37.03 he crossed the Paghman range by a mountain path to Kapiśī.
quote: Hiuan-tsang a suivi de bout en bout — sauf à la sortie de Bâmyân : de quoi il fut puni en se perdant — la grand-route de Bactres à Taxila
note: Adds to an open question: Foucher puts Xuanzang off the Shibar highway, i.e. on the Hajigak/Unai side (and, with Hackin, over the Paghman range), which favours the study's Hajigak/Unai alternative.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Begram is the capital of Kapiśa that Xuanzang saw; two walled quadrangles (Burj-é-'Abdullah and a second 'royal city')
evidence: Visit of 1923: ramparts, coins (Indo-Greek to Muslim), stupa parasol and door jamb. Above all, the hostage monastery 3 li E fixes the site.
quote: car il représente la capitale du Kapiça qu'a vue Hiuan-tsang
note: Agrees (Begram). Foucher keeps the Kapiśī highway apart from Kabul.

author: A. Foucher
name_in_asr: Couvent des otages chinois; Kôh-é-Pahlavân / Kôh-é-Tôp
asr_identification: the stupa on the southernmost spur of the isolated hill E of Begram (Kôh-é-Pahlavân, Kôh-é-Tôp)
evidence: Direction and distance (3 li E, on the S slope of a hill) and the one stupa standing on the S spur; the monastery court is c. 30 × 40 m.
quote: « Situé, nous dit Hiuan-tsang, à environ 3 li à l'Est de la cité et sur le versant Sud d'une montagne » … nous apercevons en effet vers l'Est une unique fondation bouddhique debout sur l'éperon le plus méridional d'une colline isolée
note: Agrees with Koh-i-Pahlvan. Foucher names a specific ruin (the stupa on the S spur, called Kôh-é-Tôp), which bears on the study's 'which ruin is uncertain'; he does not mention Shotorak.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: a deserted site S/SE of Begram, near the Bari-âb (Koh-daman stream)
evidence: Field survey of 1923; the description of the site itself falls in a gap of the OCR (V-1 pdf 0150/0151).
quote: stûpa de Rahula, nous avons trouvé des ruines assez intéressantes. Sur la rive nord du Bari-âb … jusqu'au site déserté du *stûpa* de Rahula
note: Consistent with a site SE of Begram (study: Kafir Qaleh / Borj-e Kafir); the exact ruin cannot be checked here because of the OCR gap.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: 1923: the ruins on the dasht of Tataranzar, S of Begram (40 li)
evidence: Distance and direction from Xuanzang (40 li S) and the ruins strewn on the dasht.
quote: Enfin un peu plus au Sud (à 40 li de la cité, nous dit Hiuan-tsang) les ruines dont est parsemé le dasht de Tataranzar se rapportent selon toute apparence à l'ancienne ville nommée par le pèlerin Si-pi-to-fa-la-sseu
note: Source of Mizutani's Tatarānzar (the study's first candidate); but see F016 for Foucher's later view.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: 1925: the large mounds of Paitâvâ and Bulandi-é-Padshahî (off the Jebel-Serâj road after Qarâbâgh) mark the town; the name is Iranian (Pahl. spêt 'white')
evidence: Visit of Oct. 1925; Hackin's excavation at Paitâvâ (Dec. 1924) found a stupa base faced with carved schist. On p. 365 the first syllables are read as Iranian spêt rather than Skt. śveta.
quote: aux tertres importants de Paitâvâ et de Bulandi-é-Padshahî qui, selon toute apparence, marquent (et ils sont loin d'être les seuls) le site de Si-pi-to-fa-la-sseu
note: Differs from the study: Mizutani's 'Tatarānzar (Foucher)' is Foucher's 1923 view. In 1942 he puts the town at Paitâvâ / Bulandi-é-Padshahî in the Koh-daman, a third candidate besides Tatarānzar and Kuwayama's Tapa Skandar.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Kanishka's great stupa = the Tôp-Darrah stupa near Charikar
evidence: Fine workmanship, drum over 75 m round, position at the mouth of gorges that produce the floods of the nāga legend; the only monument that fits.
quote: tout invite à y reconnaître l'édifice dont la tradition attribuait la fondation à Kanishka. C'est en tout cas le seul monument qui réponde aux descriptions du pèlerin
note: Agrees (Top-Darrah); this is the source of Mizutani's identification.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the easternmost of three small hills W of the Koh-daman stream, shaped like a crouching elephant's forequarters; Pilu-sâr = Iranian 'elephant's head'
evidence: The hill's shape; an elephant protome on Kāpiśī coins of Eukratides/Antialkidas (Rapson). He reads the name as Iranian (pîl-sâr).
quote: une vague ressemblance avec l'avant-train d'un éléphant accroupi au bord de l'eau … on y chercher cette colline de Pilu-sâr que Hiuan-tsang signale, mais sans indication de distance, « au Sud-Ouest de la capitale »
note: Agrees (the eastern of three hills); adds the coin and etymological arguments.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the city-goddess of Kāpiśī on an Eukratides coin sits between a hill and an elephant protome, the two sacred sites Xuanzang names near the city
evidence: Coin read by Rapson ('Kaviçi'), Euthydemos restruck by Eukratides.
quote: la divinité protectrice de la ville est assise entre les symboles des deux sites sacrés que ce dernier notera dans son voisinage
note: Supports Kāpiśī = Begram and an early cult at the Pilu-sâr hill.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Lampāka = Laghmān, reached from Kāpiśī by the direct road SE via Nijrâo, Tagâo and the Bâdpash pass, not via Kabul; here Xuanzang enters 'North India'
evidence: Rode the route in Oct. 1925 (stupas along it, a marble liṅga at Tagâo). It is shorter and has only one pass (Bâdpash, c. 1,600 m).
quote: la vieille route non carrossable de Kāpiçī à Nagarahāra … note qu'il franchit en entrant au Lampaka « la frontière de l'Inde du Nord »
note: Agrees (Laghman). Adds the route: Kapiśa → Lampāka directly SE, not through Kabul.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: no capital named; Buddhist foundations at the Alingar–Alishang confluence (Shâmatî) and large mounds near Mandrâwar below the confluence (one of Alexander's Nikaia)
evidence: Field visit Oct. 1925.
quote: Mais combien l'intérêt historique de tous ces tertres pâlit-il devant ceux qui, en aval du confluent et sur les deux rives, recouvrent probablement, près de Mandrâwar, l'une des Nikaia d'Alexandre
note: Leaves the capital open, as the study does. The Mandrâwar mounds are the study's (Vivien) alternative, but Foucher ties them to Alexander, not to Xuanzang.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the city in the SW suburb of Jalalabad, where local tradition keeps an old 'Bégrâm'; not at the Surkh-rûd confluence (Simpson)
evidence: Located from two fixed points: the shadow cave (20 li SE) at Syâh-sang and Hi-lo = Hadda (30 li SE). Six weeks in the field in 1923; given as provisional.
quote: la détermination de ces deux points de repère suffirait déjà à situer Nagarahâra dans la banlieue Sud-Ouest de la ville actuelle, là même où la tradition locale conserve le souvenir d'un ancien « Bégràm »
note: Agrees (Begram/Dasht-i-Begram SW of Jalalabad); adds the reasoning from the two fixed points.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the Dīpaṅkara stupa (3 li E, SE in the Life) may be the Ahin-Pôsh tope
evidence: Bearing (the Life's SE fits better), its hemispherical mass (dome over 75 m round) on the cliff edge, likeness to the Dharmarājikā at Taxila; Simpson's 1879 coins of Domitian, Trajan and early Kushans show a 2nd-c. rebuilding. Given as a working hypothesis.
quote: il vaudrait la peine d'examiner si le grand stûpa, fondé par Açoka à l'Est de la vieille capitale — la Biographie de Hiuan-tsang dit au Sud-Est, ce qui, en l'hypothèse, serait plus exact — ne serait pas simplement le gros « tope » aujourd'hui connu sous le nom d' « Ahin-Pôsh »
note: Agrees with the study's first candidate (credited to Higuchi); Foucher 1923 is the earlier source.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the shadow cave is at the Syâh-sang gap S of Chahâr-bâgh; the cave itself cannot be found
evidence: Faxian, Songyun and Xuanzang agree; c. six monasteries and twelve stupas within 500 m. The conglomerate cliffs have collapsed.
quote: les témoignages concordants de Fa-hien, de Song Yun et de Hiuan-tsang nous conduisent de façon sûre le long des falaises méridionales jusqu'à la coupure de Syâh-sang (la Pierre-Noire), au Sud du village de Chahâr-bâgh
note: Agrees (Syah-sang, exact cave unknown).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Hadda, 7–8 km S of Jalalabad
evidence: Name and position; Foucher's trial excavation in a quadrangle by the Teppeh-Kalân (1923) found small stupas and stucco sculpture.
quote: Or Hi-lo est aujourd'hui représenté, sans contestation possible, par le village de Hadda
note: Agrees.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the old city lies under Peshawar City, which has not moved; the old road came in via Takkal from the Khyber
evidence: Route: the Khyber road became the highway once Peshawar was founded (Kushan period).
quote: l'autre gagnait par Takkal l'emplacement de la vieille ville, aujourd'hui Peshâwar-City; car celle-ci, par exception, ne nous a pas semblé avoir changé de place
note: Agrees (Peshawar).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Prang–Chârsadda–Râjar, at the old Swat confluence
evidence: Follows Cunningham; the Kabul river's former northern channel led to the old Swat junction.
quote: C'est là, sur l'emplacement encore marqué par les villages de Prang, de Chârsadda et de Râjar que s'élevait, comme l'a bien vu Cunningham, la vieille capitale gandhârienne
note: Agrees (Charsadda/Prang).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Shahbaz Garhi, on the old road E from Pushkarāvatī via Hoti-Mardân; explains the arc Purushapura–Pushkarāvatī–Po-lou-cha–Udabhāṇḍa
evidence: Aśoka's Shahbaz Garhi edict on the old road; the road kept to the irrigated plain and avoided the Mairah dunes.
quote: la vieille ville de Po-lou-cha — dont une inscription d'Açoka, dite de Shâhbaz-Garhî, atteste l'antiquité indienne
note: Agrees (Shahbaz Garhi).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Und (Ohind, Wayhand), the traditional Indus crossing above Attock, where Xuanzang crossed both ways; the winter capital of the king of Kapiśa
evidence: Names in the Rājataraṅgiṇī, al-Bīrūnī and local usage; the river is broad and fordable there in winter; Babur forded there.
quote: Hiuan-tsang celui d'Udaka-bhânḍa, Al-bîrûnî celui de Wayhand, les gens de Peshâwar celui d'Ohind … C'est précisément là que Hiuan-tsang a fait de même, à l'aller en barque
note: Agrees (Hund/Ohind).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the spring of Hasan Abdal (Panja Sahib)
evidence: Two stages from the Indus across the Chach plain; the spring is still venerated.
quote: Dans la fraîcheur de ces eaux jaillissantes résidait jadis le roi des Nâgas Elâpatra
note: Agrees.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: three successive Taxilas; Sir-Sukh is the Kushan city, about as old as Purushapura
evidence: Marshall's excavations. He does not say which city Xuanzang saw.
quote: On n'en compte pas en effet moins de trois … Quant à la ville de Sir-Sukh, bâtie un peu plus tard par les nouveaux maîtres Kushâns de l'Inde du Nord
note: Consistent with the study's Sirsukh, but adds no argument for it.

author: A. Foucher
name_in_asr: « Grand Trésor de l'Inde du Nord »
asr_identification: not yet identified
evidence: He meant to look for it in Dec. 1918 but was prevented.
quote: celle (non encore identifiée) du « Grand Trésor de l'Inde du Nord »
note: Foucher leaves it unidentified; the study's Baoti Pind stupa (Marshall) is later.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Varṇu of Pāṇini (Bannu), but a larger country that also takes in the Gomal, Zhob and Kandar valleys; reached from Laghman in 15 days S over the Safed Koh and up the Kurram
evidence: The Life's itinerary (Laghman → 15 days S); the 4,000 li circuit; the later march of 2,000 li NW to Jāguḍa, which implies the caravan went S as far as Dera Ghazi Khan.
quote: au pays de Pa-na (transcrit ici Fa-la-na), c'est-à-dire au Varṇu ou Vārṇava de Pāṇini … embrassait également (au moins dans la nomenclature du pèlerin) les vallées du Gômal (Gômati) et de ses deux grands affluents, le Zhôb (Yayvāvati) et le Kandar
note: Agrees on Bannu as the core; extends the country S to the Gomal/Zhob basin.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the Kaikânân/Kikân of the Arab chroniclers: the Brahui country round Mastung and Kelat, S of the Bolan pass
evidence: Position (an independent wedge between Gedrosia, Arachosia, A-p'o-kien, Fa-la-na and Sind), horse- and sheep-breeding, and the Arabic name.
quote: joint à la situation géographique du district, achève de nous faire reconnaître, sous l'appellation … de Ki-kiang-na que lui donne Hiuan-tsang, le Kaikânân, Kaikân et Kikân des chroniqueurs arabes. C'est le vieux pays brâhûî
note: Differs: the study (Mizutani) has Waziristan W of Bannu; Foucher puts 稽疆那 far to the SW in NE Baluchistan (Kelat–Mastung).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Jāguḍa = Jaghuri, the upper Arghand-âb valley; reached by 2,000 li NW from the Dera Ghazi Khan latitude over the Toba-Kakar range and the Ghazni–Tarnak valley (perhaps via Kelat-é-Ghilzai)
evidence: Name (Jaghuri on the maps, a Hazara tribe in Elphinstone); route and bearing of the Life; the 7th-c. N–S road Arachosia–Kapiśa ran up the Arghand-âb.
quote: Or, grâce à une chance extraordinaire, ce pays figure toujours sur nos cartes sous le nom à peine défiguré de Jaghuri. C'est aujourd'hui la haute vallée de l'Arghand-âb
note: Differs: the study (with the route tests) centres 12.01 on Ghazni; Foucher puts the country W of Ghazni in the upper Arghandab (Jaghuri) and doubts that Ghazni belonged to it.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: doubts Hao-si-na = Ghazni: possible linguistically, uncertain geographically; one should first look for a Ghaza/Ghazna in the Arghand-âb valley
evidence: Geography of his Jāguḍa (upper Arghandab); Pelliot's note that the phonetic equivalence 'ne va pas de soi' (Tang shu gives the other capital as A-so-ni).
quote: Devons-nous, par suite, ainsi qu'on le fait généralement, identifier Ghaznî avec le Hao-si-na que le pèlerin nous donne comme l'une des deux capitales du pays ? Linguistiquement la chose est possible ; géographiquement rien n'est moins certain
note: Differs: questions the Ghazni identification the study accepts; no alternative site given.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: second capital unlocated (its spring should identify it); doubts that the upper Helmand (Lo-mo-yin-tou) belonged to Jāguḍa
evidence: Leaves both open for lack of fieldwork.
quote: à déterminer le site de la seconde capitale, Hao-sa-la, que sa source jaillissante devrait permettre de localiser à coup sûr … rattacher d'office au Jâguda, après les vallées de Ghaznî et de Tarnak, celle du haut Helmand, par le détour de son identification avec celle du Lo-mo-yin-tou de Hiuan-tsang
note: Leaves 12.01b (Guzar) and 12.01c (Helmand) open; doubts rather than rejects them.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Mount Aruṇa was shown to Xuanzang from afar at Kāpiśī; Śuna's later temple in Jāguḍa lay where the Helmand leaves the mountains
evidence: Xuanzang's two passages on the god; Śuna read as a name of Śiva.
quote: qu'on lui montre de loin le sommet du Mont-Rouge (Aruṇa) sur lequel le dieu résidait jadis … de Jâguda, de l'autre côté du massif afghan, vers l'endroit où le fleuve Hélmand sort des montagnes
note: Puts the 12.01 sanctuary near the Helmand's exit from the mountains (consistent with 12.01c), but gives no site for Aruṇa (study: Khair Khana, Kuwayama).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: in the Hazarajat: the S slope of the Koh-é-Bâbâ, where the Helmand, Kabul-rûd and left-bank Logar tributaries rise; the name survives in 'Ujaristân'; SE corner of the later Gharjistan
evidence: Route: c. 500 li N from the Arghand-âb sources via Dasht-é-Nâwar and the Bokan pass into the upper Logar/Khavat (Wardak); then NE into the Kabul-rûd valley and E to Kapiśa. Name (Ujaristân); a 'Turkish' king read as a Hazara.
quote: sur le versant méridional de la grande chaîne du Kôh-é-Bâbâ, dans la région où s'enchevêtrent les sources de l'Hélmand, du Kâbul-rûd et des affluents de gauche du Logar … l'Ujaristân de la carte anglaise nous conserve de son côté une autre déformation du nom originel
note: Differs: the study takes the country as the Koh-daman round Opian or Kabul; Foucher puts it SW of Kabul in the Hazarajat/Wardak, outside the Kapiśa plain.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: questions Opian (N of Charikar): the capital of Vṛjisthāna should lie some 30 leagues further S
evidence: Follows from his location of 12.02 and the Life's route (Vṛjisthāna → NE → E to the borders of Kapiśa).
quote: du fait qu'il existe dans le Nord du Kapiça un village du nom d'Opiân, sommes-nous en droit d'interdire rétrospectivement au pèlerin de rencontrer dans son Vriji-sthâna, à trente lieues plus au Sud, un chef-lieu dont le nom aurait ressemblé à Hou-pi-na
note: Differs: casts doubt on the sound-match Hupian/Opian that the study rates high, on route grounds; he proposes no site.

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the pass = Khāvak (descent NW leads into the Andar-âb); approach from Paghman N past Istâlif, Opîân, Tutam-Darrah, Parvân, Gul-behar
evidence: The text's NW descent; the route along the E foot of the Paghman range and the S side of the Hindu Kush. K'iu-lou-sa-pang (Life), where the king left him, is placed near Paghman.
quote: L'indication qu'il redescendit du sommet en direction du « Nord-Ouest », invite à identifier de préférence ce col avec celui de Khâvak … de toute façon la descente le conduisit dans la vallée de l'Andar-âb
note: Agrees (Khawak pass; Andarab).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the capital may be the alluvial plateau just E of the Governor's house near Banu (14–15 li round, as in the text); the Kishnabâd spur 3–4 km below is only a qaleh
evidence: Visit of 1923–24: substructures of river pebbles in the cliffs, old coins, size matching Xuanzang's figure; the valley below is too narrow for a town.
quote: Assurément, le grand plateau alluvial situé immédiatement à l'Est de la maison du Gouverneur et dont les falaises découvrent des substructions bâties en cailloux roulés, peut représenter le site d'une ancienne ville … que lui attribue Hiuan-tsang (14 à 15 li, soit près d'une heure de tour)
note: Adds a site for the capital, which the study does not have (Andarāb, Doshi valley).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Khost on the way NW from the Andar-âb to Kunduz; not the Khost W of the Kurram
evidence: Route bearing NW; his n. 32 notes a road parallel to Yarm–Narin, a little further E.
quote: Pour gagner la capitale du Houo il passa … par le pays de K'ouo-si-to, c'est-à-dire de Khost
note: Agrees (Baber's Khost).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: Kunduz, seat of the Turkish viceroy (son of the Khagan) on both of Xuanzang's visits
evidence: Biography and Memoirs: on the way out he went straight from the Iron Gates to Kunduz, stayed over a month, then went to Balkh.
quote: il se trouvait alors à Kunduz, qui, « n'ayant pas de prince particulier », était le siège de son gouvernement
note: Agrees (Kunduz).

author: A. Foucher
asr_identification: the onward route through Badakhshan, Wakhan and the Pamirs (Marco Polo's road), not followed
evidence: Not discussed further.
quote: par le chemin que devait également prendre Marco Polo et où nous n'avons pas à le suivre, à travers le Badakhshân, le Wakhân et les Pâmirs
note: No identification; no bearing on the study.
